title: Lamb and Mint Pie
subtitle: A deep shortcrust pie of braised lamb mince with fresh mint and peas
excerpt: Lamb mince and frozen peas in a thick, well-seasoned gravy with fresh mint, baked under a shortcrust lid until golden. A proper supper pie that slices cleanly and reheats well.
sourceNotes: British supper pie tradition, pairing lamb and mint in a shortcrust pastry case.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices, wrapped tightly. Reheat from frozen at 180C for 30 minutes until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the filling a day ahead and chill. Assemble and bake the next day for a crisper base.

content.text: This pie keeps things straightforward: lamb mince cooked in a light gravy with plenty of mint, cooled completely before it goes into the pastry. The filling must be cold and thick enough to hold its shape when sliced, so let the gravy reduce properly before you assemble.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Melt the butter in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onions and carrot and cook for 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to high. Add the lamb mince and cook for 8 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned all over with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 minute to coat the mince.

Pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon. Stir in the peas and mint. Season with salt and black pepper. Tip into a wide tray to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish with a small overhang. Roll the remaining pastry for the lid. Chill both for 20 minutes.

Spoon the cold filling into the pastry case. Brush the rim with beaten egg, lay the lid over the top, and press the edges firmly to seal. Trim any excess. Cut a small slit in the top and brush all over with egg.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep gold and the filling is piping hot. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.cause: The filling was still warm when it went into the case, or the gravy was too thin.
items.fix: Always cool the filling completely before filling. Bake on a preheated baking tray to help the base set quickly.

items.symptom: The lid shrank and slid off during baking.
items.cause: The pastry was not chilled before baking.
items.fix: Chill the assembled pie for at least 20 minutes in the fridge before it goes into the oven.

items.cause: The mint was added while the filling was still hot, cooking off its brightness.
items.fix: Add mint only once the filling has cooled to warm. Reserve a few fresh leaves to scatter over just before serving.
